title: Public Address System Test Sheet
source: spec/Public_Address_System_Test_Sheet.html — a one-page sheet: a banner carrying Client and Location, a title block with the drawing number and the instruction "To check ALL PA Announcement are audible", one location-by-location audibility table, a combined remarks/instruments box and a three-row sign-off. The supplied file was saved with a completed record in it (Apple South Asia Pte Ltd; AMK 2&3 (Infra Project); drawings KEN-24-0065-P2-EL-602_1 & KEN-24-0065-P2-EL-601; row 1 reading "Pls refer to attached Drawing"); those are record values, not template values, and are not carried here.

sections.title: To check ALL PA Announcement are audible
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is the grouping idiom: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same as `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`.

The source's instruction line — "To check ALL PA Announcement are audible" — is the section title rather than a field: it is fixed wording on the paper, not something a record fills in, and a section title is where this library already carries a sentence (see the ACMV pressure test's PART 4 heading).

**The two sound-level columns are `text`, not `number`.** A dBA reading is a figure, but the supplied record writes "Pls refer to attached Drawing" into the Location, Ambient and PA cells where the levels are marked up on the drawing instead — a numeric column would refuse the record this sheet is actually issued with, and matching the original wins (CLAUDE.md). The unit still prints, so a bare figure reads as dBA. Worth confirming against the paper master before Rev A hardens.

No pass/fail `limit` is declared. The paper states no acceptance criterion — the usual one is a margin over ambient, which differs by project — so the engineer's own Pass/Fail call is the result, and inventing a bound here would fail rows the consultant would accept.

The source's Pass/Fail dropdown is Pass / Fail / N/A with a blank default; the outcomes make a Fail derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6).

The source seeds eighteen blank rows and grows by cloning the WHOLE sheet — its "+ Add page" button copies header and sign-off too, purely to get more rows, then renumbers the S/N across pages. Here the table grows and the record stays one document with one sign-off; `min_rows` is eight and the engineer adds what the walk-round needs, so a record with ten locations prints ten rows rather than ten plus eight empty ones.

sections.title: Remarks / Instruments Used
sections._note:
A `field_group`, as on `lighting-circuit-test.json`: a `standard` section always prints its serial and remarks columns, so a lone textarea row comes out as an empty serial column plus two columns both headed Remarks. The source is a plain ruled box; this prints as one.

The box is the paper's only record of the sound level meter used — it heads REMARKS/INSTRUMENTS USED and gives no instrument table — so no `instruments` block is declared. When the record↔instrument linking lands (`lib/calibration.ts`), this template will want a proper instrument section rather than a prose box.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would print a one-page source on two sheets. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`.

The source's three rows, and it heads the lower two identically — "Witnessed By" — so the roles read the same here; the distinct `stage` values are what drive the workflow (SPEC §6).

The paper's sign block carries only Name, Signature and Date — no company column. The renderer always prints Company, so Tested By defaults to Kenyon Pte Ltd and stays editable (unlocked, as on `staircase-pressurization.json`); the witness companies are left blank for whoever attends.
